Package index

  • Resample and fit — %bootreg

    • Start here. Fits a model on each of many bootstrap replicates and records which terms each one kept. PROC= becomes the fitter argument, and a term the model did not select is left missing — which is what makes the counts downstream read as selection frequencies.

    boot_select()
    Build a model by bootstrap resampling

  • Summarise the replicates — %SUMBOOT and %cluster

    • Reach for these once you have replicates. boot_summary() gives the per-variable selection frequency and coefficient distribution; boot_clusters() answers the question it cannot — how often at least one member of a correlated group survived. Both are held to exact parity with the macros.

    boot_summary()
    Summarise bootstrap replicates into selection frequencies
    boot_clusters()
    Aggregate selection frequencies over clusters of correlated variables

  • Report over a screen

    • The model-agnostic reporting layer, extracted so that the logistic, linear, Cox and hazard bootstrap reports are thin templates rather than near-copies of one another. boot_validate() checks that the screen a runner wrote has the shape a report reads; the rest turn it into tables. The ones that group their rows take an optional phase, so a multiphase hazard screen and a single-phase logistic screen run down the same code path; boot_dropped() and boot_health() have nothing to group and take none. boot_bag() is the way in from this package’s own screen: boot_select() returns a wide object and everything here reads a long one.

    boot_bag()
    A screen the reporting layer can read
    boot_validate()
    Check that a bootstrap bag has the shape a report reads
    boot_provenance()
    Where a bootstrap screen came from
    boot_seeds()
    Every seed a bootstrap screen used
    boot_frequencies()
    Selection frequencies, with the error they carry
    boot_dropped()
    Candidates the screen never saw
    boot_concepts()
    Selection frequencies grouped by concept
    boot_health()
    Did the bootstrap screen actually run?

  • Pool a chunked run

    • Needed only when a screen was run in chunks, which is how a run of days is made restartable. boot_pool_chunks() folds them into one object of the same shape, refusing to pool chunks that did not draw from the same data or run the same screen; boot_shortfall() says whether what you pooled is the run you launched, which nothing inside a chunk can know.

    boot_pool_chunks()
    Pool chunked bootstrap runs into one screen
    boot_chunk_files()
    Find the chunk files of a chunked bootstrap run
    boot_shortfall()
    Is a pooled screen the run that was launched?

  • Fitters — one per PROC=

    • Passed to boot_select(), one per model family. Use these when choosing the model type; write a new one when adding a family, rather than a new pipeline. Each returns the coefficients its model kept, or NULL when the fit failed and the replicate should be redrawn.

    fit_linear()
    Fit a linear model for one bootstrap replicate
    fit_logistic()
    Fit a logistic model for one bootstrap replicate
    fit_cox()
    Fit a Cox proportional-hazards model for one bootstrap replicate

    Package overview

    The shape of the port: three macros and three functions at the core, with the pooling and reporting layers that grew around them.
